title: Daemon boot under host load: the OMP probe exits the process and the supervisor loops it; one worker's reconnect error aborts every other reconnect

spec.contract: Acceptance items 1-3 and 5-7, plus the Design, Errors and Testing sections. Item 4 (revokeRoleClaim never dereferences api before it exists) is LEGION-11's and is NOT implemented here.

requiredSkills.implement: legion-worker (bookmark legion/LEGION-28, `Dispatch: LEGION-28` in the PR body, READY-format PR body, handoff commit discipline) and test-driven-development (every behaviour change below lands with the named test written first, red, then green).
requiredSkills.test: legion-worker (fill the PR body's E2E section with the real-daemon run in `acceptance7Recipe`, one negative control) and verification-before-completion (log lines and pane lists are the evidence, never the unit tests).
requiredSkills.review: legion-worker (thermonuclear-deep-review and thermonuclear-code-quality once at the reviewed head; every thread dispositioned individually; verify CI/E2E facts on GitHub) and receiving-code-review (the launch-hold and per-claim isolation are load-bearing concurrency changes: verify, do not accept claims).

legion11Pr.title: fix(daemon): probe workers after the API starts so a dead worker's cleanup no longer crashes on restart
legion11Pr.state: OPEN, reviewDecision REVIEW_REQUIRED, mergeable CONFLICTING against main
legion11Pr.head: legion/LEGION-11 @ 7dccf39852e7 (change rxsqswlv, 'test: record handoff')
legion11Pr.forkPoint: 8f6fad367099 'chore: release pi-envoy v1.4.3' — 36 main commits behind; main has since added packages/daemon/src/daemon/boot-probes.ts (#966), worker-stream-listener.ts (#967) and rewrote 261 lines of index.ts

baseBranch.decision: Do NOT `jj new legion/LEGION-11`: that head predates boot-probes.ts (the file this issue changes), conflicts with main, and carries LEGION-11's own .legion/*.json handoffs, which our later phases would misread as their predecessors. Instead, base on `main` and bring LEGION-11's one source commit along as a duplicate so item 4's ordering is present without re-implementing it.
procedureAtImplementationStart: CASE A — #955 merged: work on top of this issue's plan-handoff commit as-is (it is a child of main); after `jj git fetch`, `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" rebase -s <plan-handoff commit> -d main` if main moved. No duplicate.

CASE B — #955 still open (expected): duplicate LEGION-11's fix commit onto this issue's plan-handoff commit: `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" duplicate 'legion/LEGION-11 & description(glob:"fix(daemon): run reconnectWorkers after the API exists*")' -d <plan-handoff commit>` (at plan time this is change lxkxplmnvusm / commit 82b191d26f5f: index.ts moves `reconnectWorkers` + `pruneSecretFiles` + the pending-controller-notice block after `api = startLegionApi(...)`, and adds the index.test.ts test 'retires a ready-confirmed worker whose shim socket is dead at boot'). Verified in a scratch clone at plan time: this duplicate applies onto current main with NO conflict and lands `reconnectWorkers` after the worker-stream listener block and before `enableWorkerPromotion()`. Do NOT duplicate LEGION-11's docs commit (pvvslolyryvy 'docs(daemon): comments and invariants follow reconnectWorkers…') — it conflicts with main's AGENTS.md (adjacent-insertion conflict at the end of 'Operational invariants') and this issue rewrites that same boot-ordering paragraph anyway; nor its plan/implement/test handoff or docs/plans commits.

Then `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" new <duplicate>` and implement on top. Keep `.omp/config.yml` (provisioning scaffold present in the working copy) out of every `jj split`; set `legion/LEGION-28` at the last logical commit, never at the working-copy remainder.
baseBranch.prBody: The PR body states, in plain words: 'Depends on #955 (LEGION-11: probe workers after the API starts so a dead worker's cleanup no longer crashes on restart). Commit <sha> is a duplicate of that pull request's fix so item 4's boot ordering is present here; review from commit <first LEGION-28 sha> on. This pull request must merge after #955.' The `Chain:` line of the READY format reads `stacked on legion/LEGION-11 (duplicated fix commit) — not frozen; rebased onto main by the merger once #955 lands`.
baseBranch.mergerProcedure: Once #955 has merged: `cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git fetch`, then `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" rebase -s <plan-handoff commit> -d main --skip-emptied` — the chain is main → plan handoff → duplicated LEGION-11 fix → LEGION-28 commits; rebased onto a main that already contains LEGION-11, the duplicate empties out and `--skip-emptied` drops it (nothing of value is abandoned; never run `jj abandon` by hand). If LEGION-11 landed with a differently-worded fix, the duplicate keeps a residual diff instead of emptying: resolve toward main's (LEGION-11's merged) text. Expect one small AGENTS.md conflict where LEGION-11's 'Boot ordering' bullet and this issue's rewritten bullets meet: keep this issue's text (it supersedes LEGION-11's bullet). Re-run `bun test packages/daemon packages/workspace` and `bunx tsc --noEmit`, push, wait for CI, and re-verify the approved head before publishing READY.

plannerVerifications.check: (1) jj git clone into a temporary sibling directory, then rename into place, still works
plannerVerifications.result: PASS. jj 0.45.1 (this machine). `jj git clone <repo> $T/target.tmp-abc` then `mv $T/target.tmp-abc $T/target`: `jj -R $T/target log`, `jj status`, and `jj workspace add $T/ws1` all succeed in the moved directory; `.jj/repo/store/git_target` is the relative `../../../.git`. The only absolute paths under `.jj` are inside op_store operation records (the recorded command lines of past operations — informational, never resolved). Both the colocated default and a plain clone behave the same. `jj git clone` also accepts an existing EMPTY destination directory (so `mkdtemp` may create the temp dir), and `fs.rename` onto an existing non-empty directory fails with ENOTEMPTY (the collision case below relies on this). No completion-marker fallback needed.

plannerVerifications.check: (2) how a spawn arriving during the probe hold is queued — exact hook
plannerVerifications.result: Today `WorkerAdmission.launchOrQueue` (worker-admission.ts ~L273-303) decides inside `withAdmissionLock` on `runningWorkerCount() >= config.workerCap` only, and `resumeOrQueueExisting` (~L352-384) on `client.runState !== 'idle' || runningWorkerCount() >= cap` only — neither consults `workerPromotionEnabled`, so a `spawnWorker` during boot with a free slot launches a pane today. The hold adds `!this.workerPromotionEnabled` to BOTH decisions: the not-admitted branch already does `enqueueClaimForLaunch`/`enqueueIdleWorker` → `persist()` → `publishArchitect({type:'worker-queued'})` → returns `queued` (`spawnWorker` maps the second to `{status:'queued'}`). Promotion: `ProcessManager.reconcileWorkerAdmission()` → `WorkerAdmission.reconcileWorkerAdmission()` → `drainWorkerQueue()` → `promoteQueuedWorker()`, already gated on `workerPromotionEnabled` (~L712-720) and already the call boot makes right after `enableWorkerPromotion()`. `enqueueForRetry`/`enqueueForRetryPending` (retire path) already push while gated and rely on the same drain. `promoteWorkerQueue()` already no-ops with the log 'worker-queue promotion trigger ignored: not yet enabled (still booting)'. Roots have no such gate today: `ProcessManager.admit()` (processes.ts ~L400-428) calls `startRoot` directly when `admission.active.length < cap`, and `advancePromotionSweep()` (~L1902-1931) launches queued trees; `resurrect()` (~L1736) and `ensureController()` (~L1396) open panes too. Task 4 below adds the root-side gate.

plannerVerifications.check: (3) existing index.test.ts tests that pin the bounded five-attempt retry and the blocking boot order
plannerVerifications.result: See task 6's `testsThatChange`: 'rejects an OMP invocation without pi.agents before accepting daemon work' (asserts loadState never ran and NATS never started — both now happen), 'retries a boot probe whose launch died transiently, then boots once it passes' (asserts sleeps [5000, 15000]), 'does not retry a definitive pi.agents negative, and gives up after the last transient retry' (asserts 6 attempts and sleeps [5000,15000,45000,90000,180000]; createNatsTransport throws), 'rejects an installed pi-legion-envoy that omp does not actually load (disabled or unregistered) before accepting daemon work' (loadState/NATS never ran), 'names the real cause when the configured launch prefix itself fails the plugin-load probe…' (createNatsTransport throws). Also scripts/smoke/README.md line 86 ('The daemon must refuse before state, NATS, or its API starts') and the boot-probes.ts header comment ('The two probes `startDaemon` runs before it owns state or serves the API'). cli/__tests__/index.test.ts's probe-image tests keep passing (bounded policy) — one new bounded-timeout test is added there.

design.runnerTimeout: `CommandRunnerOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (default stays 30_000). `CommandResult` gains `readonly timedOut?: { limitMs: number; elapsedMs: number }`, present ONLY when the runner's own kill timer fired (`proc.kill()` → SIGTERM; Bun resolves `proc.exited` with 143 for a SIGTERM kill — verified on bun 1.3.14 here). `elapsedMs` is wall time from spawn to exit measured with `performance.now()` (it includes any time a child kept the stdio pipes open after the kill — truthful, and why the probes use `exec`). No caller may report a kill as `Command failed (exit N)` again.
design.probeRetry: boot-probes.ts: `interface ProbeRetryPolicy { initialDelayMs; maxDelayMs; maxAttempts?: number }` with delay for the i-th failure = min(initialDelayMs * 2^i, maxDelayMs). Exported policies: `DAEMON_PROBE_RETRY = { initialDelayMs: 10_000, maxDelayMs: 300_000 }` (no maxAttempts: unbounded) and `IMAGE_PROBE_RETRY = { ...same, maxAttempts: 6 }` (bounded: 10+20+40+80+160 s ≈ 5 min worst case) plus `IMAGE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000`. Both `verifyOmpAgentsCapability` and `verifyLegionPluginLoaded` take one options object `{ sleep, timeoutMs, retry }` instead of the trailing `sleep` argument; each runner call passes `{ timeoutMs }`. Classification: `result.timedOut` → transient (before any marker logic); otherwise unchanged (marker present + non-zero exit → transient; `missing` marker, clean exit without marker, or launch failure before OMP → definitive). Log per transient attempt: `[legion] <name> probe failed transiently (attempt N); retrying in <delay>s: <detail>` (append `/M` to N only when maxAttempts is set); a timeout's detail is `command timed out after <limit> s (ran <wall> s)` plus any stderr tail. Exhausting maxAttempts throws makeError(detail) exactly as today.
design.bootOrdering: startDaemonLocked (index.ts), on top of LEGION-11's ordering: (1) environment, runner, Dispatch token file; (2) `const probes = (async () => { await verifyOmpAgentsCapability(...); await verifyLegionPluginLoaded(...); })(); probes.catch(() => {});` — started, not awaited (the no-op catch prevents an unhandled-rejection crash if a definitive negative lands before the hold; the real handling is at the hold); (3) tokenManager.getToken, state load, gate-off handling, NATS, ProcessManager, event pump, API, worker-stream listener, `reconnectWorkers`, `pruneSecretFiles` — exactly as on the LEGION-11-duplicated base; (4) THE HOLD: hoist `stopped`/`resyncTimer`/`lingerTimer` and the `stop` closure above this point (the timers it clears are still undefined there — guard `lingerTimer !== undefined`), then `try { await probes; } catch (error) { try { await stop(); } catch (teardown) { console.error('[legion] teardown after a failed boot probe failed:', teardown); } throw error; }` — `stop()` already stops the event pump, disposes the ProcessManager, drains the pending save, closes the worker stream, the API and NATS, and releases the instance lock (idempotent — `startDaemon`'s own catch releases it again harmlessly). `startDaemon` therefore still REJECTS with the probe's error on a definitive negative; `import.meta.main` and `legion start` exit 1 as today. (5) `processManager.enableLaunches(); processManager.reconnectRoots(); await processManager.reconcileAdmission(); await processManager.reconcileWorkerAdmission(); await processManager.replayHeldRecoveries();` then the pending-controller-notice drain/spawn block (moved here from before the hold: `ensureController` opens a pane), then timers, signal handlers, handle. `startDaemon` resolves only after the hold releases and boot admission has settled — unchanged contract for every caller. Known consequence (accepted): `legion start` writes the legions-registry entry only when `startDaemon` resolves, so `legion status <team>`/`legion stop <team>` do not see the daemon while the probe is still retrying; the API port is known from config and answers, and the supervisor owns the process. Rejected alternative: resolving `startDaemon` before the probe passes (a background hold releasing later) — needs a second failure channel (`deps.exit(1)` after a resolved start), a cancellable probe sleep so `stop()` during the hold does not wait out a 5-minute backoff, and every definitive-failure test rewritten; nothing in the spec requires it.
design.launchHold: ProcessManager gets one boot gate: `private launchesEnabled = false`, `enableLaunches(): void` (renames today's `enableWorkerPromotion()` via lsp rename — it sets `launchesEnabled = true` and calls `this.workerAdmission.enableWorkerPromotion()`; `WorkerAdmission.enableWorkerPromotion()` keeps its name as the worker-side internal). While closed: `admit()` treats the cap as full (`admission.active.length >= admission.cap || !this.launchesEnabled` → status `queued`, pushed to `admission.queue`, persisted, returns 'queued'); `advancePromotionSweep()` treats the cap as full the same way (clears the sweep when nothing is in flight, persists, returns); `WorkerAdmission.launchOrQueue`/`resumeOrQueueExisting` enqueue when `!workerPromotionEnabled` (see verification 2) → `spawnWorker` returns `{status:'queued'}` and `worker-queued` is published — this also covers `resumeWorker` (exception/404 recovery) since it goes through `spawnWorker`; `resurrect(treeKey)` records the key in `private readonly heldResurrects = new Set<IssueKey>()`, logs `[legion] resurrection of <tree> held until the OMP probe passes`, and returns; `ensureController()` sets `private heldControllerRequest = true`, logs `[legion] controller launch held until the OMP probe passes`, and returns. `replayHeldRecoveries(): Promise<void>`: for each held tree `await this.resurrect(tree)` (catch → `console.error('[legion] held resurrection of <tree> failed:', error)`), then `if (heldControllerRequest) await this.ensureController()` (catch → log), clearing both. Everything that only stops/kills panes (`closeTree`, `beginLinger`, `stopProcess`) or talks to pre-existing panes (`workerReady`, `controlDirective`, `markTreeReady`) is NOT gated — the hold is about opening panes, and a pane that survived the restart is not ours to hold. The processes.test.ts `manager()` helper's `skipEnablePromotion` option becomes `skipEnableLaunches` and calls `enableLaunches()`.
design.reconnectIsolation: `reconnectWorkers`: the body of the `claims.map(async ([token, claim]) => { … })` callback is wrapped in `try { … } catch (error) { console.error(`[legion] failed to reconcile worker ${token}:`, error); }` — `Promise.all` over never-rejecting promises awaits every claim; a throwing claim is left exactly where the throw found it (e.g. `revokeSessionCapability` throwing inside `retireWorkerLocator` happens before `delete current.locator`, so its locator stays). `reconnectRoots`: same per-tree wrap around `armRootRegistrationDeadline` with `[legion] failed to reconcile root ${tree.root}:`. index.ts keeps its outer `catch` + 'worker reconnection failed' log as the last resort (LEGION-11's test asserts that line never appears for a dead worker).
design.config: `slow_command_timeout_seconds` / `LEGION_SLOW_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` → `DaemonConfig.slowCommandTimeoutSeconds`, `DEFAULT_SLOW_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300`, following `worker_rpc_timeout_seconds` exactly: CONFIG_SCHEMA key, the `readPositiveInteger` file mapping tuple, `resolveValue(cli, file, parseEnvPositiveInteger(env.LEGION_SLOW_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, 'LEGION_SLOW_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS'), default)`, membership in `lifecycleNumbers` (so `slowCommandTimeoutSeconds must be a positive integer` refuses startup), and the field on the returned config. Used as `config.slowCommandTimeoutSeconds * 1000` for both boot probes' `timeoutMs` and as `ProvisionIssueWorkspaceDeps.commandTimeoutMs`. Every `DaemonConfig` literal in tests gains `slowCommandTimeoutSeconds: 300` (ci-fixtures.ts, index.test.ts `config()`, processes.test.ts, processes.thermo-ops.test.ts, real-shutdown-e2e.test.ts).
design.workspaceProvisioning: workspace.ts: `RunResult` gains `readonly timedOut?: { limitMs: number; elapsedMs: number }`; `WorkspaceCommandOptions` gains `readonly timeoutMs?: number`; `ProvisionIssueWorkspaceDeps` gains REQUIRED `readonly commandTimeoutMs: number`; a single `run(deps, cmd, opts)` helper passes `{ ...opts, timeoutMs: deps.commandTimeoutMs }` to every `deps.run` call (the direct `deps.run` calls in `createWorkspace` included), and `runChecked` throws `Command timed out after ${limitMs/1000} s (ran ${(elapsedMs/1000).toFixed(1)} s): ${cmd.join(' ')}` (stderr appended on a new line when non-empty) when `result.timedOut` is set, else the existing `Command failed (exit N)` message. `ensureRepoClone`: if the final dir exists WITH `.jj` → return; if it exists WITHOUT `.jj` → `console.error(`[legion] removing incomplete clone at ${repoCloneDir} (no .jj) before cloning again`)` and `rm -rf` it; then `mkdir -p` the parent, `tempDir = await mkdtemp(`${repoCloneDir}.clone-`)` (a sibling in the same parent, so the rename is a same-filesystem directory move), `jj git clone <remote> <tempDir>` through `runChecked`, verify `<tempDir>/.jj` exists (else throw `Incomplete Jujutsu clone at <tempDir>: missing .jj`), then `rename(tempDir, repoCloneDir)`. Any throw between mkdtemp and a successful rename → `rm(tempDir, {recursive, force})` then rethrow. Rename collision (ENOTEMPTY/EEXIST — two issues provisioning the same repo for the first time concurrently): if `<repoCloneDir>/.jj` now exists the other clone won → remove own temp dir and return; otherwise rethrow. Leftover `<repo>.clone-*` siblings from a daemon crash are inert (they can never be mistaken for a clone) and are NOT swept — a sweep would race a concurrent in-flight clone. processes.ts `provisionWorkspace` passes `commandTimeoutMs: this.deps.config.slowCommandTimeoutSeconds * 1000`; `ProcessManagerDeps.run`'s result type gains `timedOut?` (the wrapper already spreads `...result`, and `createDaemonRunner` already spreads options, so `timeoutMs` reaches `defaultRunner` unchanged).
design.probeImage: cli/index.ts `cmdProbeImage` passes `{ sleep: deps.sleep, timeoutMs: IMAGE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, retry: IMAGE_PROBE_RETRY }` to both probes — bounded, because an image build has no supervisor and must finish.

tasks.commit: feat(daemon): the command runner takes a per-call timeout and reports a kill as a timeout

tasks.commit: fix(daemon): a boot probe killed at its budget is retried with capped exponential backoff, never a crash loop

tasks.title: Launch hold: nothing opens a pane until enableLaunches(); spawns queue
tasks.change: See design.launchHold. Rename `ProcessManager.enableWorkerPromotion` → `enableLaunches` with the LSP (callers: index.ts, processes.test.ts helper + ~10 tests). Rewrite `WorkerAdmission.workerPromotionEnabled`'s doc comment (it now also turns a fresh spawn into a queued one during boot's probe hold) and the stale 'before `api` exists' sentences in worker-admission.ts (~L122-128, ~L327-330) and processes.ts (`retireUnconfirmedBoot` doc ~L912-916).
tasks.tests: processes.test.ts (all built with `skipEnableLaunches: true`): (a) 'queues a root admitted and a worker spawned while launches are held, and launches both once enableLaunches() runs': `admit(root)` → 'queued', `state.admission.queue` = [root], `state.trees[root].status` = 'queued', no tmux `new-window`; `spawnWorker(root, root, 'tester', task)` → `{status:'queued'}`, `state.workerAdmission.queue` includes the tester token, a `worker-queued` publication, no `new-window`/`split-window`; then `enableLaunches(); await reconcileAdmission(); await reconcileWorkerAdmission()` → root active with a `new-window`, tester launched with `worker-started`. (b) 'holds a resurrection and a controller launch requested during the hold, and replays both after enableLaunches()': an active tree whose recorded pane is dead (list-panes returns nothing) — `await resurrect(root)` opens no window and the error log names the tree; `await ensureController()` opens no window; `enableLaunches(); await replayHeldRecoveries()` → a `new-window` for the root (resumed with `--resume` of its recorded session file) and one for the controller. Existing boot-ordering tests 'mints nothing for a queued worker when an idle reconnect fires onIdle before enableWorkerPromotion…' (~L7294) and the two `skipEnablePromotion` reconnect tests (~L8867, ~L8968) are renamed to the new option/method, semantics unchanged.
tasks.commit: feat(daemon): a launch hold queues every spawn until boot releases it

tasks.title: Per-claim reconnect isolation
tasks.tests: processes.test.ts 'a throw while reconnecting one worker claim is logged with its token and leaves that claim alone while every other claim is reconciled': three ready-confirmed claims (planner/tester/reviewer on one root) with locators (pane ids %1 %2 %3, session ids ses-1 ses-2 ses-3, distinct socket paths); `connectWorkerRpc` rejects ECONNREFUSED for all three; `revokeSessionCapability` throws `new TypeError('api.revokeSessionCapability is not a function')` when called with 'ses-2'; `spyOn(console,'error')`. Assert: `await processes.reconnectWorkers()` resolves; claims 1 and 3 have `locator` undefined and `resumeSessionFile` set, and `kill-pane` ran for %1 and %3; claim 2 still has its locator with pane %2 and no `kill-pane` for %2; one error log whose first argument contains `failed to reconcile worker <token2>` and whose second is the TypeError. Cheap sibling for `reconnectRoots`: three active unconfirmed trees with locators, an injected `sleep` that throws synchronously on its second call → `reconnectRoots()` does not throw, `sleep` was called three times, one log names the second tree.
tasks.commit: fix(daemon): one worker's reconnect failure no longer aborts every other worker's reconnect

tasks.title: Boot ordering: probes start first, awaited only at the launch hold; definitive failure exits 1 after closing the API and NATS
tasks.change: See design.bootOrdering. Rewrite the two boot comments that currently explain the pre-API `reconnectWorkers` position and the 'Awaited only now that api is assigned' block so they describe the hold. Pass `timeoutMs: config.slowCommandTimeoutSeconds * 1000` and `retry: DAEMON_PROBE_RETRY` to both probes.
testsThatChange: 'rejects an OMP invocation without pi.agents before accepting daemon work' → rename to '…refuses to serve: exits after closing the API and NATS it had opened'. Keep `rejects.toThrow('does not expose pi.agents')` and the probe argv assertions; replace `loadedState toBeFalse` / `natsCreated toBeFalse` with: state WAS loaded, a FakeNats WAS created and `nats.closed === true` afterwards, and the instance lock is released (a second `startDaemon` with a passing runner works — pattern from 'refuses to start when worker_stream_port is bound…').
'retries a boot probe whose launch died transiently, then boots once it passes' → sleeps `[10_000, 20_000]`, attempts still 4.

'does not retry a definitive pi.agents negative, and gives up after the last transient retry' → keep the two definitive sub-cases (give `baseDeps` a FakeNats instead of a throwing `createNatsTransport`); DELETE the bounded give-up sub-case and replace it with 'keeps retrying a transiently failing probe past the old bound with the backoff capped at five minutes': the pi.agents probe fails transiently 7 times then passes → sleeps `[10000,20000,40000,80000,160000,300000,300000]`, 8 pi.agents attempts + 1 plugin attempt, daemon boots.

acceptance7Recipe.surface: A real daemon process on the smoke rig (`scripts/smoke/up.sh`) or an equivalent local `bun run packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts start <project> --config <legion.yaml>`.
setup: Write an executable wrapper, e.g. /tmp/legion28-hang-probe.sh: `#!/bin/sh` / `count_file=/tmp/legion28-probe.count` / `n=$(cat "$count_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0); echo $((n+1)) >"$count_file"` / `if [ "$n" -lt 2 ]; then exec sleep 60; fi` / `exec "$@"`. `exec sleep` matters: a `sleep` child that survived its parent's kill would hold the runner's stdio pipes open and the 'kill' would only return after 60 s.

Export `LEGION_SLOW_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=5` (env beats the default; the generated legion.yaml does not set the key) and `SMOKE_OMP_LAUNCH_PREFIX="/tmp/legion28-hang-probe.sh secrets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY GEMINI_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY --"` (the wrapper goes FIRST so it wraps the whole launch; `up.sh` writes it into `omp_launch_prefix`, which the daemon prepends to both probes and every pane). Remove any stale /tmp/legion28-probe.count. Run `up.sh`.

Expected timeline: probe attempt 1 killed at 5 s → `[legion] OMP pi.agents probe failed transiently (attempt 1); retrying in 10s: command timed out after 5 s (ran 5.0 s)`; attempt 2 killed → `…(attempt 2); retrying in 20s…`; attempt 3 passes (wrapper count ≥ 2); the plugin probe passes; then the queued root launches.
evidence: During the hold (within the ~40 s window): `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:$LEGION_DAEMON_PORT/legion/v1/state | jq '.trees, .admission'` → 200 with the root queued; `tmux -L legion-<project> list-panes -a` → no panes (or the tmux server is not running); `daemon.log` shows the two attempt lines with their delays.

After: `daemon.log` shows no further probe failures, the root's `new-window`, and `/legion/v1/state` shows the tree active with a locator; `tmux -L legion-<project> list-panes -a` shows the root pane.

Negative control: point `LEGION_OMP_PATH` at a wrapper that prints `LEGION_OMP_AGENTS=missing` and exits 0 → the daemon logs `[legion] daemon failed: … does not expose pi.agents`, exits 1, and `/legion/v1/state` refuses connections afterwards (the API was closed before exit). Attach the log lines and both pane lists to the PR body's E2E section.

risks: The hold is a new gate on every pane-opening path; a path missed keeps launching during the hold. Reviewer checklist: `admit`, `advancePromotionSweep`, `resurrect`, `ensureController`, `WorkerAdmission.launchOrQueue`, `WorkerAdmission.resumeOrQueueExisting` are the only callers that reach `spawnRoot`/`launchWorker`/`spawnController` (verified by grep at plan time: `startRoot` ← admit/advancePromotionSweep; `spawnRoot` ← startRoot/resurrectDeadTree; `launchWorker` ← launchOrQueue/promoteQueuedWorker; `spawnController` ← ensureController).

`legion status`/`legion stop` cannot find the daemon while the probe is still retrying (registry entry written when `startDaemon` resolves). Accepted; recorded in AGENTS.md. If the architect wants the entry earlier, that is the rejected background-hold design and a scope change.

During the hold no SIGTERM handler is installed yet (they are registered after the hold, as today after the probes); a supervisor stop during the hold kills the process immediately — no panes exist yet to stop gracefully, and the durable lane saves before it acks, so nothing is lost beyond an at-least-once redelivery.

A clone killed by SIGTERM may leave a `jj` child (`git` helper or askpass) holding the pipes briefly; `elapsedMs` reports the truth. If the tester sees a provisioning kill take far longer than its budget, the fix is a SIGKILL escalation in `defaultRunner` — out of this issue's scope, name it as the one fast-follow.
